Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. Ben and Lily are preparing a report about the train station. She sent a postcard from Paris.

Lily ordered dumplings and coffee at the travel plan last night. Little by little, things began to change. The train station looked quieter than usual that evening. Also, a tailback formed after the accident.
At first, Lily found it difficult to keep the habit. The travel plan has become an important part of daily life. Lily's dream job is to be a doctor. We booked a hotel near the beach.

The experience taught Lily more than any book could. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. People around Lily often share different ideas about the train station. What's more, families with infants get priority boarding.
Ben always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Lily wrote down every idea in a small notebook. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on.
